transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. I'm Dr. [Name]. What brings you in today?

I'm... just having a hard time lately. I guess I can't really shake this heavy feeling. It's like a mix of being scared and... feeling guilty. I just feel tense most of the day, like I'm waiting for something else to go wrong. And I just keep blaming myself for not stopping what happened.
Have you been feeling down or losing interest in things you usually enjoy?
I don't know. I guess I just... haven't really felt like doing much.
Have you noticed that you’re not enjoying things that you usually like to do, or that you’ve lost interest in them completely?
I guess... yeah. I just don't really have the energy for much of anything right now. It's just easier to stay home.
Do you find yourself feeling overly watchful or on edge, like you're constantly alert for danger?
I'm not really sure... I mean, I guess I'm a little jumpy sometimes, but I haven't really noticed being constantly on edge or anything. I just... I don't know.
Have you gone through any particularly stressful or traumatic event recently that might be contributing to how you're feeling now?
...Yeah. I guess so. It's been... about four months. My husband, um... he had a fall while we were doing a porch repair. It's just been going on since then.
Have your symptoms stayed about the same since your husband's accident, or have they gotten better or worse over time?
I'm not really sure... I haven't really been keeping track of it. I guess it mostly just feels the same. I don't know.
Looking back, would you say your symptoms have stayed pretty much the same since your husband's accident, or have there been times when they were noticeably better or worse?
Um... like I said, I'm really not sure. I haven't noticed it being noticeably better or worse or anything. It mostly just feels like it's been the same. I don't really pay that close attention to it.
Since your husband's accident, have you found yourself thinking about it a lot, or having trouble getting it out of your mind?

...Yeah. Sometimes. I mean... with my job, if I'm just measuring a railing or I hear a ladder scrape somewhere... it kind of just comes out of nowhere. I'll see him falling again, like it's happening right in front of me. My stomach drops, and... my hands get kind of shaky. So, um... yeah. I guess it's hard to get it out of my mind.
Since your husband's accident, have you found yourself avoiding certain places, activities, or situations because they remind you of what happened?

Um... I guess a little. Like with work, I've been trying to pass on jobs if they have... like, raised porches or second-story decks. I just let someone else take those now. And... at home, I just sort of find excuses to not talk about the repair. I don't really want to look at the spot where it happened. So... yeah.
Since your husband's accident, have you noticed yourself having negative thoughts about yourself or the world, or feeling a lot of guilt or blame related to what happened?

...I guess. I just... I keep thinking about how I missed it. At my own house. It makes me feel like... maybe I'm not as careful or competent as I thought I was. Even though my work reports don't show any issues, I just... yeah. I guess I've been hard on myself about it.
